outcomes.text: Answer comprehension questions requiring answers of differing lengths on a non-literary Urdu text of approximately 400 words.
R1: Understand and convey information.
R2: Understand, order and present facts, ideas and opinions.
R3: Evaluate information and select what is relevant to specific purposes.
R4: Recognise implicit meanings and attitudes.
Write one composition of 300–400 words in response to a choice of argumentative, discursive, descriptive and narrative titles, each taken from a different topic or sub-topic.
Write an argumentative composition of 300–400 words.
Write a discursive composition of 300–400 words.
Write a descriptive composition of 300–400 words.
Write a narrative composition of 300–400 words.
W1: Present relevant facts, ideas and opinions in an engaged manner and using appropriate detail.
W2: Articulate relevant experience and express what is thought, felt and imagined.
W3: Show a sense of audience and an awareness of appropriate register and style.
W4: Order, develop and link facts, ideas, opinions and arguments (structure).
W5: Exercise control of a range of appropriate grammatical structures (language).
W6: Understand and accurately employ a range of appropriate vocabulary (language).

topics.title: Topic areas (Part 1 Reading passage and Part 2 Writing titles)

subtopics.title: Health and fitness; the world of youth

outcomes.text: Read and write on topic area 1, Health and fitness: e.g. food and diet, sport.
Read and write on topic area 2, The world of youth: e.g. music, traditional and modern culture, technology, fashion, family.

subtopics.title: Education and training; the world we live in

outcomes.text: Read and write on topic area 3, Education and training: e.g. school and college, work, professions.
Read and write on topic area 4, The world we live in: e.g. current affairs, the environment, travel and tourism, the media.
T1: Demonstrate first-hand knowledge of the content of literary texts, through close reference to details and use of quotations from the text.
T2: Understand the literal meanings of texts and the contexts of those meanings.
T3: Understand literary texts beyond their literal meanings in terms of the issues and attitudes they raise.
T4: Recognise and appreciate ways in which writers use language to create their effects of narration, description, characterisation and literary structure.
T5: Communicate an appropriate and informed response to what is read.

Show an informed and appropriate personal response, sometimes asked directly (e.g. 'What do you think?', 'What are your feelings about … ?') and sometimes by implication (e.g. 'Explore the ways in which …').
Show understanding of themes, characters, relationships, situations, issues and attitudes.
Show understanding of the writer's intentions and methods, including use of language.

Read an extract (from poetry or prose) not seen before and answer one passage-based question testing critical understanding of the text and response to the ways in which the writer achieves effects, using the prompts the question gives (there are no set texts for Part 1).
Study the ghazals of Khwaja Haider Ali Ahtish: 'Hawae dur mah e Khush Gawar raah main he' and 'Sun to sahi jahan men hai tera fasana kya'.
Study the ghazals of Parveen Shakir: 'Ko ba Ko phail gaee baat shanasaee kee' and 'Tarash ker miray bazoo Uran choor gaya'.
Study the ghazals of Momin Khan Momin: 'Aser uss koo zara nahin hota' and 'Thani thee dil mai abb nah milain gay kisee say Ham'.
Study the ghazals of Allama Iqbal: 'Kabee ah haqeeqat muntazir nazar Ah ja lebaas' and 'Khirad mand oon say kiya phochoon ky maree abtada kiya he'.
Study the ghazals of Ahmed Faraz: 'Tum bhee Khafa hoo loog bhee berham hain dostoo' and 'Silsilay tor gaya who sabhi jaate jaate'.

Study Altaf Hussain Hali, Musadas Hali (17 selected stanzas), stanza 1 'Kisee nay buqraat say ja kay poocha …', stanza 2 'Sabab yaa alamat ger un koo samjain …', stanza 3 'Yahee haal duniya mai uss qoom kaa he …' and stanza 4 'Gata ser pay udbaar krr chaa rahee he…'.

Study Musadas Hali stanza 5 'Per uss qoom ghafil kee ghaflat wahee he …', stanza 6 'Kaheen tha mawashee caranay pay jagrah …', stanza 7 'Joo hotee thee payda kisee ghar main dukhtar …' and stanza 8 'Jo un kee din raat kee dil lagee thee …'.

Study Musadas Hali stanza 9 'Yakayaq huwee gharat Haq koo herkat …', stanza 10 'Huway mahw alam say Asaar zulmat …', stanza 11 'Woo nabiyoon mai rahmat laqab panay wala …' and stanza 12 'Khata kar say der guzar kernay wala …'.

Study Musadas Hali stanza 13 'Misay Kham koo jis nay kundan banaya …', stanza 14 'Pharee kaan mai daat thee ik nikami …', stanza 15 'Woo fakhr e arab zeb mahraab o mimber …', stanza 16 'Kaha sab nay Qul Aaj tak koee tara …' and stanza 17 'Kaha taree her baat kaa yaan yaqeen he …'.
Study Syed Zameer Jafree's nazm 'Admee'.
Study Mirza Mahmood Sarhadi's 'Qitaat': 1 'Tamam zer kay …', 2 'Kabee tou in …', 3 'Jis kaa bas …', 4 'Qaim kuch aisay …', 5 'Nokree kay liyee …', 6 'Bay khaber abb …'.

subtopics.title: Prose articles: Azad, Baig, Abbas, Qasmi

outcomes.text: Study Rishta Nata by Muhammad Hussain Azad.
Study Imtahaan by Mirza Farhatullah Baig.
Study Overcoat by Ghulam Abbas.
Study Shafarish by Ahmad Nadeem Qasmi.

subtopics.title: Prose articles: Sir Syed, Yousafi, Taj

outcomes.text: Study Umeed kee Khushi by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
Study Ur ahna ghar mai murgiyoon kaa by Mushtaq Ahmed Yousafi.
Study Ahraam o Sakoon by Syed Imtiaz Ali Taj.
Study Mirza Ghalib's Khatoot e Ghalib letter 1, Ba Naam Her Gopal Tifta: 'Allah Allah! Ham tou … Maray kahnay ur likhnay kee kiya Hajat?' (Charshamba 3 November 1858).
Study Mirza Ghalib's Khatoot e Ghalib letter 2, Ba Naam Mir Mahdi Majroo: 'Bhai! Kiya poochtay hoo? kiya likhoon?' … 'Yousaf e Hind Mir Afzal Ali koo Dua' (2 December 1859).
